summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fatigue, somnolence, and rigors in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He was found to have coagulase-negative staph bacteremia, likely originating from his port, though no clear source was identified. He was treated with a week of IV vancomycin and will complete a 14-day course at home with nursing support. During admission, he developed transient groin pain, which resolved without intervention, and a new systolic murmur attributed to anemia, with echocardiogram ruling out endocarditis. Altered mental status was linked to hypoglycemia and opioid use; insulin regimen was adjusted with endocrinology input. A small subgaleal hematoma was incidentally noted on head CT with no clinical significance. He received one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia and was discharged in stable condition with plans to resume chemotherapy after antibiotic completion.
